source.jql: project = SCRUM AND issuetype = Requirement ORDER BY key ASC

requirements.approved_text: The project shall produce design documentation that describes the construction and operation of the temperature measurement system.
The project shall produce a prototype demonstrating that the proposed design functions.
The final system shall satisfy the applicable stakeholder requirements or document an approved stakeholder change for any deviation.
Ambiguous or conflicting stakeholder requirements shall be clarified before the affected design is finalized.
The system shall consist of a computer, two temperature-sensor assemblies, a battery-operated third-box assembly, and support for delivery of text messages and/or email to a receiving device.
Temperature information produced by the third-box thermometer shall be accessible through an internet-connected computer while the required system components are operational.
The sensor assemblies, third box, cables, controls, and connectors shall satisfy the stakeholder-specified physical construction, handling, drop, and connection requirements.
The system shall tolerate temperature-sensor disconnection and reconnection without requiring user intervention to restore normal operation.
The third-box power switch shall control availability of local thermometer functionality and current remotely accessible temperature data.
The system design shall support temperatures from at least -10 deg C through +63 deg C.
The temperature-measurement system shall visibly respond to sensor heating under the stakeholder-specified hand and soldering-iron tests.
The thermometer shall satisfy the specified room-temperature and ice-water measurement tolerances.

requirements.summary: SYS-HLR-400 - Local Temperature Display and Controls
requirements.approved_text: When powered ON, the third box shall display temperature information according to the independently controlled display state of Sensor 1 and Sensor 2.
The third-box display shall present correct temperature information with the required response time and indoor readability.
The third box shall notify the local user when a temperature sensor is disconnected or otherwise malfunctioning.
When the computer software and third box are operational, the system shall provide remotely accessible real-time temperature/status information for both temperature sensors.
The computer user shall be able to remotely enable or disable the local third-box temperature display for each temperature sensor, with a response in less than one second.
If the computer software is already running while the third box is OFF, required temperature information shall become available within 10 seconds after the third box is turned ON.

The computer interface shall provide a chart-recorder-style graphical representation of the most recent 300 seconds of temperature data with the specified units, axes, missing-data behavior, and scrolling behavior.
When the computer and third box are ON, the system shall send configurable text and/or email notifications when real-time temperature exceeds a configured maximum or falls below a configured minimum.
At laboratory room temperature, the thermometer output shall be approximately 22 deg C +/- 4 deg C.
When a sensor is placed in a water-ice mixture, the thermometer output shall be 0 deg C +/- 2 deg C.

requirements.summary: HWE-MLR-200 - Sensor Quantity and Cable Length
requirements.approved_text: The hardware shall provide two temperature sensors, each at the end of a 1.0 +/- 0.1 meter cable.
The sensor assemblies shall tolerate ordinary handling and placement in ice water without damage.

requirements.summary: HWE-MLR-202 - Third-Box Enclosure and Drop Survival
requirements.approved_text: The third box shall be enclosed and shall remain functional after the specified workbench-to-floor drop and upside-down operation.
External cable connectors shall be securely mounted, casual-user connectable, and shall not break during the specified connected-cable drop.
The sensor electrical interface shall permit powered connection and disconnection without damaging the sensor or third-box electronics.
The third box shall contain a battery and physical ON/OFF power switch and shall operate as a standalone battery-powered thermometer.
The third box shall be designed around an ESP32 microcontroller capable of running the required firmware and BLE interface.
The third-box local display shall be a character LCD with variable backlight brightness.
The third box shall provide one local physical means of adjusting LCD backlight brightness using either a button-based control or a potentiometer.
Each sensor shall connect to the third box through a USB-C termination, and Sensor 1 and Sensor 2 ports shall be visually distinguishable.

The custom sensor USB-C interface shall be electrically arranged or protected so that foreseeable accidental connection of a standard USB-C cable or power source does not damage the third box or sensor.
The LCD hardware shall support all characters required to display sensor labels, OFF/DISCONNECTED/error indications, signed temperatures across the required range, and the average value.
The selected sensors and associated electrical interface shall support the required temperature range and sufficient accuracy to meet the end-to-end accuracy requirements.
Each completed sensor cable assembly shall measure between 0.9 m and 1.1 m from the third-box connector interface to the sensing element.
The sensor head and exposed cable region intended for immersion shall use insulation/encapsulation suitable for temporary immersion in an ice-water mixture.
The ESP32 board/module, LCD, battery, connectors, and other internal assemblies shall be mechanically retained so they do not become loose during the required drop test.
Internal wiring and mounted parts shall not depend on gravity or enclosure orientation for electrical continuity.
Each external cable connector shall be panel-mounted or mechanically supported independently of PCB solder joints.
Sensor cable assemblies shall include strain relief at the probe end and connector end.
Sensor input circuitry shall tolerate insertion/removal transients without requiring a third-box reset.
The battery and regulator path shall supply the simultaneous peak current required by the ESP32, BLE radio, LCD/backlight, and both sensor interfaces.
The power switch shall remove or disable operating power such that the ESP32/LCD cannot continue providing current temperature data when the switch is OFF.
The selected ESP32 device/module shall include BLE capability supported by the selected ESP-IDF version.
The character LCD shall be electrically interfaced to the ESP32 using the selected supported digital interface and shall provide enough character positions to render the required local states.
The backlight circuit shall support more than two discernible brightness levels without exceeding the LCD backlight current rating.

requirements.summary: HWE-LLR-212 - Backlight Control Input - Button Option
requirements.approved_text: If the button option is selected, the backlight control shall provide a debounced ESP32 digital input used to step through defined brightness levels.

requirements.summary: HWE-LLR-213 - Backlight Control Input - Potentiometer Option
requirements.approved_text: If the potentiometer option is selected, the backlight control shall provide an ESP32 ADC-readable voltage spanning the usable control range.
Sensor 1 shall terminate in a dedicated USB-C receptacle/plug pair assigned to the Sensor 1 electrical interface.
Sensor 2 shall terminate in a dedicated USB-C receptacle/plug pair assigned to the Sensor 2 electrical interface.
The enclosure shall use permanent labels, symbols, or other visual differentiation to identify Sensor 1 and Sensor 2 ports.
The custom sensor connector design shall prevent an accidental standard USB-C VBUS connection from applying damaging voltage to sensor-signal pins or the ESP32.
Custom sensor signals shall not be exposed on standard USB-C pins in a way that can damage a standard USB host/device during foreseeable accidental connection.
The physical display size shall permit rendering at least a sensor identifier/state and a signed temperature value within -10 to +63 deg C.
The selected sensor datasheet shall specify an operating/measurement range that includes -10 through +63 deg C.
The hardware error budget at 0 deg C and approximately 22 deg C shall leave sufficient margin for software conversion/rounding while meeting the stakeholder tolerances.
Third-box firmware shall be implemented for the ESP32 using ESP-IDF and the C programming language.
The third-box firmware shall continuously acquire readings/status from both temperature sensors while powered ON.
The third box shall maintain separate rolling buffers containing the last 300 one-second records for Sensor 1 and Sensor 2.
The third box shall expose three user-visible states per sensor: ON, OFF, and DISCONNECTED.
A disconnected/faulted sensor shall be reported as DISCONNECTED while the fault exists and shall return to the OFF display state after a valid reconnection unless the user subsequently enables it.
The firmware shall independently control whether Sensor 1 and Sensor 2 temperatures are shown on the LCD.
When both sensor display states are ON and both readings are valid, the LCD shall display Sensor 1, Sensor 2, and the average of the two readings.
The firmware shall update the LCD to reflect a local sensor-display control action within approximately 20 ms.
The firmware shall render a clear local fault/disconnected indication instead of a valid temperature for an unavailable sensor.
The firmware shall support variable LCD backlight brightness using the selected physical backlight input.
The third-box LCD shall present temperature values in degrees Celsius and support signed values across the required system range.

The firmware shall provide an internally consistent current snapshot containing both sensor values, sensor states, display-enable states, average validity/value, and sample identity for a computer request.
Sensor acquisition shall automatically resume after reconnection without restarting the ESP32 firmware.
The firmware shall accept validated remote commands that change the same sensor display-enable state controlled by the physical sensor buttons.
The ESP-IDF application shall initialize sensor drivers, LCD/backlight drivers, input handlers, shared state, history buffers, and the BLE service from app_main().
Firmware shall maintain one runtime record per sensor containing latest temperature in Celsius, validity/connection state, display-enabled state, and the latest sample sequence number.
The sensor acquisition task shall begin a new read for each sensor whenever the previous read cycle is complete and shall update the shared runtime record only after validating the result.
A read failure on one sensor shall not skip or block acquisition of the other sensor.
A periodic timer/task shall snapshot each sensor runtime record into its history buffer once every 1000 ms.
Each sensor history buffer shall be implemented as a fixed-capacity circular buffer of 300 records; adding record 301 shall overwrite the oldest record.
Each stored history record shall contain at least the sample sequence number, temperature value when valid, and a sensor status value sufficient to distinguish valid and missing/disconnected data.
History retrieval code shall expose records in chronological order from oldest available to newest available regardless of circular-buffer wrap position.
Firmware shall maintain sensor connection/health separately from the user display-enable flag and shall derive the externally visible ON/OFF/DISCONNECTED state from those values.
A valid connected sensor with display_enabled=true shall report ON; a valid connected sensor with display_enabled=false shall report OFF; an invalid/disconnected sensor shall report DISCONNECTED.
After the configured sensor-driver fault criterion is met, firmware shall set the sensor connection/health state to DISCONNECTED and invalidate its current temperature.
When a DISCONNECTED sensor produces a valid reading again, firmware shall mark it connected, set display_enabled=false, and expose the sensor state as OFF.
A debounced press of Sensor 1 or Sensor 2 button shall toggle that sensor display_enabled flag only when the sensor is connected.
Pressing a sensor display button while that sensor is DISCONNECTED shall not cause a valid temperature to be displayed or change the reported DISCONNECTED state.
The firmware shall calculate the displayed average as (sensor1_c + sensor2_c) / 2 using sufficient intermediate precision to avoid overflow or unnecessary rounding error.
The local average shall be valid/displayed only when both sensors are connected, valid, and their display_enabled flags are true.
Local button handling shall render from the latest cached sensor values rather than waiting for a new sensor conversion.
The local input handler shall signal the LCD update path immediately after a valid button-state change so that software scheduling does not intentionally delay the update beyond 20 ms.
For a disconnected/faulted sensor, the LCD rendering layer shall display a DISCONNECTED or equivalent clear error label instead of a numeric temperature.
For a connected sensor with display_enabled=false, the LCD rendering layer shall display Sensor 1 OFF or Sensor 2 OFF, as applicable.
Firmware shall expose a backlight-set function accepting a normalized brightness level and isolate physical-input-specific logic from LCD rendering logic.
If the button option is selected, each debounced backlight-button press shall cycle through a finite set of defined brightness levels including at least low, medium, and high.

If the potentiometer option is selected, firmware shall periodically sample the ADC input, map the usable ADC range to backlight brightness, and suppress insignificant jitter before updating the backlight.
All third-box internal temperature calculations and BLE payload temperatures shall use Celsius as the canonical unit.
The current-data response shall copy both sensor runtime records under a synchronization mechanism so one response cannot mix values from different update instants.
Firmware shall generate or increment a boot/session identifier at startup and include it with current/history metadata so computer software can distinguish samples across third-box restarts.
A successful sensor read after a disconnected period shall restore acquisition status without restarting the acquisition task, BLE service, or whole device.
Remote display commands and physical buttons shall update the same display_enabled fields and invoke the same LCD rendering path.
Firmware shall reject remote display-control requests containing an invalid sensor identifier or unsupported state value without changing local state.
The third box and computer connection component shall communicate using Bluetooth Low Energy.
The third box shall transmit application data only in response to a computer-initiated BLE request; unsolicited application telemetry shall not be required.
The BLE interface shall support a request that returns the current state and value of both sensors and the current local display state.
The BLE interface shall support validated remote commands to change Sensor 1 and Sensor 2 local display-enable states and shall expose the resulting state.
The BLE interface shall permit retrieval of both 300-record sensor history buffers from the third box.
The BLE protocol and computer client shall support automatic reconnection/recovery without requiring application restart.
The BLE interface shall use an authentication/bonding mechanism sufficient to prevent an arbitrary nearby BLE client from issuing third-box control commands.

requirements.summary: INT-MLR-407 - Protocol Versioning and Error Reporting
requirements.approved_text: The BLE application protocol shall provide protocol-version identification and explicit success/error status for commands.
The ESP32 shall expose one custom 128-bit GATT service dedicated to thermometer application communication; the computer connection process shall identify compatible devices by this service UUID.

Application temperature and history data shall be transmitted only in response to computer-initiated GATT transactions. The third box shall not transmit application temperature or history data using unsolicited GATT notifications or indications.
Each application request shall carry a request identifier, and each response shall echo that identifier so the client can match responses to requests.

Each application message shall contain at least protocol version, opcode, request identifier, payload length, and response status when applicable. Optionally, the application messages may include parity bits

The protocol shall define a GET_CURRENT request whose response includes boot identifier, newest sample sequence, Sensor 1 temperature/status/display state and Sensor 2 temperature/status/display state.
The protocol shall define a SET_DISPLAY request containing sensor identifier and desired display-enabled Boolean value.
The SET_DISPLAY response shall return success/error and the resulting externally visible sensor state.
The protocol shall define a GET_HISTORY_META request returning boot identifier, newest sequence, and available record count for each sensor buffer.
The protocol shall define a GET_HISTORY_CHUNK request containing sensor identifier, chronological starting offset/sequence, and requested record count.
A history-chunk response shall contain only complete history records and shall identify the sensor, starting record position/sequence, and number of records returned.
The history retrieval implementation shall segment the 300-record history into BLE-safe chunks and shall not assume the entire history fits in one ATT payload.

The computer BLE client shall request a larger ATT MTU when supported. If a smaller MTU is negotiated, the history transfer shall remain functional by reducing the number of complete history records included in each chunk so that each response fits within the negotiated MTU.
The protocol shall define at least SUCCESS, INVALID_COMMAND, INVALID_SENSOR, INVALID_VALUE, NOT_AVAILABLE, and INTERNAL_ERROR response statuses.
A receiver shall reject an application message using an unsupported protocol version without applying state-changing commands.
The ESP32 and computer client shall use BLE pairing/bonding with authenticated/encrypted access for state-changing characteristics/commands.
After BLE link loss, the computer client shall resume scanning/connection attempts automatically and shall not require a user to restart the web application.
The computer application shall consist of a MySQL database, a web application/server, and a third-box connection component.
The third-box BLE connection component shall run in separately (I.E: via different operating-system process or thread) from the web UI/server.
The third-box connection process shall request current data from the third box at a nominal 1 Hz rate and publish each result to MySQL.

On application startup or BLE reconnection, the connection process shall retrieve available third-box history and persist it so the most recent 300 seconds can be displayed within the stakeholder time limit.
While third-box data is unavailable, the computer software shall preserve the one-second time base and represent missing data distinctly from valid sensor measurements.
The web application and BLE process shall exchange remote third-box control requests through a defined inter-process mechanism that supports the less-than-one-second response requirement.
The connection process shall automatically detect, reconnect to, and resume polling a compatible third box after it becomes available.
MySQL shall provide persistent storage for temperature history and shared state used by the computer application.

The database shall persist one-second temperature records for three series: probe 1, probe 2, and the computed average of the two, with per-series value and status, third-box device and session identity, and sample identity. Series status shall distinguish valid readings from unplugged-sensor, no-data, provisional, and derived-unavailable conditions.
The database shall persist user roles, alert recipients/rules, and third-box control-command state required by the web application.

MySQL shall provide a durable command queue conveying control commands from the web server to the third-box connection process, together with execution status returned by that process. Verification: issue a display-toggle command via the web UI and confirm the third-box display changes in under 1 second (desired latency).

Persisted temperature values shall use Celsius as the canonical unit, with conversion to Fahrenheit performed at presentation only. This supports the user-selectable display units required by {Req 5.a} and {Req 5.c.i}, and the third-box display in {Req 4}. Temperatures shall be stored with fixed-point precision sufficient to cover the {Req 8.a} design range of −10 to +63 °C without rounding error affecting alert threshold comparisons.

Application-created timestamps shall be stored in UTC. This is a team design decision rather than a spec-derived requirement {Req 5.c.iii} labels the graph axis in relative "seconds ago" and no wall-clock time is displayed. UTC is retained because local time is not monotonic across timezone transitions, and both the history index (**SWE-DB-LLR-552**) and the time-range replacement in **SWE-CONN-LLR-509** assume ordered timestamps.
The BLE connection component shall start as an independent process/service with its own main loop and database connection.

The connection worker shall issue GET_CURRENT transactions at 1 Hz, scheduled against a monotonic clock so that sample spacing is unaffected by system time adjustments. Scheduled poll times shall not deviate by more than ±100 ms from one-second boundaries.   
  
Verification: log poll timestamps over 300 seconds and confirm the count is 300 ±1 and no interval exceeds the stated tolerance.

For each valid GET_CURRENT response, the computer BLE connection worker shall store the received sensor temperatures, statuses, display states, boot identifier, and sample sequence number in the database. The worker shall also store the UTC response-receive time and the average temperature, calculated from the same sample when both sensor readings are valid.

If a scheduled 1 Hz poll does not yield a valid reading, the worker shall persist a record for that one-second interval rather than repeating the previous value, so gaps remain distinguishable from valid data {Req 5.c.iv} and the graph continues scrolling {Req 5.c.v}.

Missed-poll records shall be marked provisional, indicating an interval for which no third-box reading was obtained and which may be superseded if that data is later recovered. The worker cannot determine at poll time whether the box is powered off or merely unreachable, so no distinction is made when the record is written. Resolution of provisional records on reconnection is specified in **SWE-CONN-LLR-509**.

Verification: interrupt the third-box connection during operation and confirm records continue to be written at 1 Hz marked provisional, with no value carried forward from the previous reading.
After disconnection, the worker shall retry compatible-device discovery/connection frequently enough that a newly powered third box is detected within 10 seconds.
The worker shall initiate a history synchronization after first connection and after reconnecting to a new boot identifier.

Before requesting history chunk data, the worker shall request history metadata from the third box, comprising: the boot/session identifier, the oldest and newest available sample sequence numbers, and the sample count available per sensor. The worker shall use this to determine which chunks are required rather than fetching blindly. If metadata cannot be obtained within \[N\] seconds, synchronization shall abort and retry rather than proceeding to chunk requests, so as not to exceed the 10-second startup budget in {Req 5.c}.

Verification: initiate synchronization with a populated third-box buffer and confirm a metadata request precedes any chunk request, and that requested chunk ranges fall within the reported available range.

Following metadata retrieval, the worker shall request history chunks until the most recent 300 seconds of available records have been obtained, or until the synchronization time budget is exhausted. The combined metadata and chunk-retrieval budget shall not exceed \[N\] seconds, preserving the 10-second startup requirement in {Req 5.c}. Individual chunk requests shall be retried up to 2 times on failure.

If the budget expires before the full 300 seconds is retrieved, synchronization shall persist the records obtained and leave the remaining interval as a gap rather than discarding partial history; gaps remain distinguishable per {Req 5.c.iv}.

Verification: initiate synchronization against a full third-box buffer and confirm 300 seconds of records are retrieved within the budget; repeat with an artificially delayed link and confirm partial history is persisted and the budget is not exceeded.

For third-box records lacking absolute timestamps, the worker shall reconstruct observation times by anchoring the newest recovered sample to the time its response was received and assigning preceding samples at one-second intervals by descending sample sequence.

Reconstructed timestamps are approximate; accumulated error across a 300-second recovery shall not exceed 2 seconds, consistent with the "seconds ago" axis labelling in {Req 5.c.iii}. Where a reconstructed timestamp overlaps an interval already covered by live polling, the live sample shall take precedence.

Verification: recover a known-length history and confirm reconstructed timestamps are monotonically decreasing at one-second spacing, that the newest aligns with the first live sample without duplication or gap, and that total span matches the recovered sample count.

On history synchronization, the worker shall upsert recovered samples keyed on device, boot, and sample identity so that repeated synchronization does not create duplicate records.

Provisional records written by **SWE-CONN-LLR-503** carry no third-box sample sequence and shall be resolved by time range rather than by upsert:

* If the recovered boot identity matches the session active before the gap, provisional records within the recovered range shall be replaced by the recovered samples.
* If the boot identity differs, the third box was power-cycled and no data exists for the gap; provisional records preceding the new session's first sample shall be reclassified as no-data {Req 5.a.ii}.

Verification: (a) synchronize history twice in succession and confirm record count is unchanged; (b) drop the connection with the box powered, reconnect, and confirm provisional records are replaced by recovered samples; (c) power-cycle the box and confirm provisional records for the off period become no-data.

The worker shall poll the control command queue at an interval not exceeding 250 ms. This bounds queue latency within the end-to-end budget for {Req 5.b}, which requires third-box display response in under 1 second: up to 250 ms queue latency, leaving no less than 750 ms for BLE command execution and third-box display update.

Verification: issue a display toggle from the web UI and confirm the third-box display changes in under 1 second, measured across ten trials.

The worker shall claim a pending command by atomically transitioning it from PENDING to IN_PROGRESS in a single conditional update, matching on both command identity and current state. The worker shall proceed with BLE execution only if the update reports one row affected; if zero rows are affected the command was already claimed and shall be skipped.

Concurrent worker instances are not supported in the current architecture. The atomic claim prevents re-execution following a worker restart or retry, not contention between instances.

On completion the worker shall transition the command to SUCCEEDED or FAILED and record completion time. Commands remaining in IN_PROGRESS beyond \[N\] seconds shall be treated as abandoned and transitioned to FAILED, so that a worker failure mid-execution does not leave a command permanently claimed.

Verification: (a) issue a command and confirm the claim transition occurs exactly once and the command reaches a terminal state; (b) terminate the worker after claim but before execution and confirm the command transitions to FAILED within \[N\] seconds rather than remaining IN_PROGRESS.
After executing a remote display command, the worker shall record command completion status, completion time, and resulting third-box state in the database.
The worker shall update a database device-state record with connected/unavailable state and last-seen time whenever BLE availability changes.
A BLE poll failure or database write failure shall be handled as an error for that cycle and shall not terminate the worker process without a controlled fatal condition.

Create a temperature_samples table containing device_id, boot_id, sample_seq, observed_at_utc, sensor1_c, sensor1_status, sensor2_c, sensor2_status, average_c, average_valid, and record_source fields.

Re-inserting a temperature sample that has already been stored shall not create a duplicate record. Uniqueness shall be enforced by a database constraint on third-box device identity, session identity, and sample sequence extended to include series identity if series are stored as separate rows. Verification: attempt to insert a record matching an existing key and confirm the database rejects it without creating a second row.

The temperature_samples table shall carry an index on (device_id, observed_at_utc) supporting the two required access patterns: retrieval of the most recent sample per series and retrieval of all samples within a bounded time window of up to 300 seconds. If series are stored as separate rows, series identity shall be included in the index. Verification: EXPLAIN on both query forms shows the index in use rather than a full table scan.

Temperature samples shall be retained for a minimum of 300 seconds after the observed timestamp. Samples older than 600 seconds shall be eligible for automatic deletion. The retention floor shall exceed the maximum user-selectable graph window (300s) with margin sufficient to avoid contention between deletion and history queries.

Create a users table containing a unique username, password hash, role, enabled state, and creation/update audit timestamps. Role shall be one of USER or ADMIN. ADMIN accounts may perform third-box control and alert configuration; USER accounts are read-only. No plaintext password is stored.

Create an alert_recipients table storing recipient type (EMAIL or SMS) and destination address. The table supports multiple recipients of each type per team design decision. Verification: insert multiple EMAIL and SMS recipients, confirm all persist and are retrievable by the alerting logic.

Create an alert_rules table storing a minimum threshold, maximum threshold, high-temperature message, low-temperature message, and the monitored series, linked to one or more alert_recipients. Verification: create a rule with both thresholds and messages, confirm all five editable fields persist and are retrievable.

Create a control_commands table storing target sensor, desired display state, requested time, execution state, completion time, and execution result. Verification: insert a display-toggle command, confirm it is retrievable in PENDING state and that state and completion time update on execution.

The control command state shall be one of exactly: PENDING, IN_PROGRESS, SUCCEEDED, FAILED, EXPIRED. A command that has not been claimed by the connection process within \[N\] seconds shall transition to EXPIRED, ensuring no command remains indefinitely pending when the third box is unavailable per {Req 5.a.ii}. Verification: insert a command with the third box powered off, confirm it transitions out of PENDING within \[N\] seconds rather than remaining queued.
All numeric threshold and temperature fields stored in MySQL shall use Celsius regardless of the user-selected display unit.

All timestamps stored in the database shall use UTC, including sample observation times, command creation and completion times, and any audit timestamps. This applies to timestamps generated by the application and to any database-generated defaults; the database server's timezone shall be configured to UTC so both are consistent. Conversion to local time is performed at presentation only, and is not required by the current UI, which labels the graph axis in relative time per {Req 5.c.iii}.
Database credentials and secrets shall be supplied through environment/configuration outside version-controlled source files.
The computer shall host a web application/server that provides the browser UI and mediates access to database-backed temperature, configuration, and control functions.
The web UI shall obtain current temperature/status data from MySQL at a nominal 1 Hz rate.
The web application shall be usable on desktop and mobile displays and shall provide user and admin roles that prevent unauthorized third-box and notification control.
The UI shall provide a settings page for configuring multiple email/SMS recipients and alert thresholds/messages.

requirements.summary: SWE-WEB-MLR-604 - Main Graph Page and Series Selection
requirements.approved_text: The main view shall be a graph page supporting simultaneous selection of Sensor 1, Sensor 2, and Average series, with current values for selected series.
The web UI shall allow the user to display real-time and historical temperatures in Celsius or Fahrenheit.
The UI shall distinguish disconnected sensors, unavailable third-box data, missing graph data, and valid off-scale graph data.
The UI shall provide an admin control page or section for remotely selecting the temperature information displayed on the third-box LCD.
The stakeholder-required graph shall use fixed limits of 10 to 50 deg C or 50 to 122 deg F.

The implementation design requests a configurable graph range within -10 to +63 deg C. This feature conflicts with the stakeholder requirement that the graph always use fixed 10 to 50 deg C limits and shall remain blocked until stakeholder approval or be implemented only as a separate non-required view.
The stakeholder-required graph shall display a total time record of 300 seconds.

The implementation design requests a selectable graph time range up to 300 seconds. This conflicts with the stakeholder statement that the total displayed record is 300 seconds and shall remain blocked until stakeholder approval or be implemented only as a separate non-required view.
The web server shall provide a read-only API endpoint that returns the latest database-backed Sensor 1, Sensor 2, average, sensor-status, box-availability, and display-state data.
The web server shall provide a read-only history endpoint accepting a requested duration up to the permitted limit and returning timestamped sensor/average values and status/missing markers.
The web server shall provide an admin-only endpoint that validates a sensor display request and inserts the corresponding PENDING control command into MySQL.
The web server shall provide an admin-authorized mechanism to read the status/result of a submitted third-box control command.
The graph/current-value client shall request current data from the web server every 1000 ms while the page is active.
When the current API reports box unavailable or sensor invalid, the browser shall replace the prior numeric current value with the appropriate status text instead of retaining it as current.
The graph, current-value cards, settings forms, and control page shall use responsive layout rules that avoid horizontal overflow at common phone and desktop viewport widths.
The application authorization model shall define USER and ADMIN roles.
A USER shall be permitted to view current temperatures and graphs but shall not modify third-box controls, alert recipients, alert rules, or privileged account settings.
An ADMIN shall be permitted to use third-box control and notification/settings functions.
The settings page shall display all configured email/SMS recipients and allow an admin to add, edit, enable/disable, and remove recipients.
The settings page shall allow an admin to configure minimum and maximum Celsius-equivalent thresholds independently for each alert recipient/rule.
The settings page shall allow an admin to edit the high-temperature and low-temperature message text associated with an alert rule.
The graph page shall provide independent controls for displaying Sensor 1, Sensor 2, and Average, and shall permit any combination of the three.
The graph page shall show a current-value indicator for each selected series and suppress or mark the average unavailable when one or both sensor readings are invalid.
The web application shall calculate or read Average only from valid Sensor 1 and Sensor 2 values from the same sample record.
The web layer shall treat Celsius database values as canonical and convert to Fahrenheit using F = C \* 9/5 + 32 for presentation.
Changing the unit selector shall update current-value labels, graph values, graph-axis labels, and configured threshold presentation without altering stored Celsius data.
For a disconnected sensor, the current-value UI shall display a textual indication of an unplugged sensor instead of a numeric temperature. I.E: “Sensor X Unplugged”
When the third box is OFF/unavailable, the current-value UI shall display the exact text "No data available" instead of a numeric temperature.
A missing/unavailable sample shall be rendered as a visible gap and/or dedicated missing marker and shall not be connected as if it were a valid temperature sample.
A valid sample below/above the visible Y-axis shall be represented differently from a missing sample, for example by a boundary/clipped indicator while preserving its valid status.
The control page shall provide independent admin controls for Sensor 1 and Sensor 2 local LCD display-enable state.
After submitting a display-control command, the control page shall update from the command result/current state rather than assuming the command succeeded.
In the stakeholder compliance graph, Celsius Y-axis minimum shall be 10 and maximum shall be 50.
In the stakeholder compliance graph, Fahrenheit Y-axis minimum shall be 50 and maximum shall be 122.
The stakeholder compliance graph shall request/render 300 seconds of history and label the X-axis in seconds ago from 300 on the left to 0 on the right.
If stakeholder approval is obtained for the design extension, an advanced/custom graph view may accept validated Celsius-equivalent Y-axis limits within -10 to +63 deg C and require min < max.
If stakeholder approval is obtained for the design extension, an advanced/custom graph view may accept a time window greater than 0 and less than or equal to 300 seconds.
The computer software shall support both email and SMS alerts and shall allow multiple configurable destinations.
Each configured recipient shall support independently configurable high and low temperature thresholds.
The high-temperature and low-temperature alert message text shall be configurable from the computer UI.
Notification delivery shall be performed by the computer through third-party email and SMS service APIs rather than by the third box.
Only valid current temperature measurements shall be evaluated against alert thresholds.

The software shall avoid sending an alert every second while a temperature remains continuously out of range; an edge/episode-based notification policy shall be used unless the stakeholder specifies otherwise.
The web application shall authenticate users and enforce role-based authorization so non-admin users cannot control the third box or notification configuration.
Each alert recipient record shall identify exactly one delivery type: EMAIL or SMS.
The alert evaluator shall process all enabled recipient/rule records applicable to a valid sample rather than stopping after the first matching recipient.
Each alert rule shall contain minimum and maximum Celsius thresholds and a monitored source identifier.
The alert evaluator shall compare each enabled recipient rule using that rule's own thresholds; one recipient's thresholds shall not alter another recipient's evaluation.
A high-threshold notification shall use the configured high-message text for the matching rule/recipient.
A low-threshold notification shall use the configured low-message text for the matching rule/recipient.
Implement an SMS provider adapter that accepts destination and message text and invokes the configured third-party SMS API using credentials supplied outside source control.
Implement an email provider adapter that accepts destination and message text and invokes the configured third-party email API using credentials supplied outside source control.
A notification-provider failure shall be logged/recorded and shall not block subsequent one-second temperature polling.
The alert evaluator shall skip a sensor/rule evaluation when the underlying sample status is unavailable/disconnected/invalid.
If Average is supported as an alert source, it shall be evaluated only when both Sensor 1 and Sensor 2 values in the same sample are valid.
For each enabled recipient/rule/source combination, maintain alert state NORMAL, HIGH, or LOW.
Send the high alert only when the rule state transitions from NORMAL/LOW into HIGH; do not resend each one-second sample while it remains HIGH.
Send the low alert only when the rule state transitions from NORMAL/HIGH into LOW; do not resend each one-second sample while it remains LOW.
Return the rule state to NORMAL when the valid temperature is between the configured minimum and maximum, allowing a later new excursion to generate another alert.
User passwords shall be stored only as a modern salted password hash; plaintext passwords shall not be stored in MySQL.
The web server shall require an authenticated session/token before serving privileged control/settings operations.
Every third-box control and alert-configuration API endpoint shall enforce ADMIN authorization on the server side independent of whether UI controls are hidden.
If cookie-based sessions are used, authentication cookies shall be HttpOnly and use appropriate SameSite/Secure settings for the deployment environment.

Server-side validation shall reject malformed phone numbers/email addresses, invalid threshold ordering, unsupported sensor identifiers, and out-of-range control values before persistence or command execution.

The implementation-decision phrase "power states of the sensors (on/off)" shall be interpreted as the third-box LCD display-enable state unless the team explicitly changes the hardware architecture; literal sensor power gating conflicts with continuous sensor acquisition and the stakeholder virtual-button requirement.
Until clarified otherwise, the control page sensor ON/OFF action shall submit SET_DISPLAY commands and shall not electrically power down the sensor.

The team shall define whether each recipient threshold applies to Sensor 1, Sensor 2, both sensors independently, and/or Average. The database and evaluator shall support an explicit monitored-source field so the choice is not implicit.
Define a monitored-source enumeration supporting SENSOR_1 and SENSOR_2 and optionally AVERAGE; each alert rule shall store exactly one source value.
The third-box LCD shall be clearly readable under normal indoor lighting conditions.

requirements.summary: HWE-MLR-214 - Display Size and Resolution Unconstrained
requirements.approved_text: No stakeholder-mandated physical display size or pixel/character resolution applies beyond the requirements to render all required information correctly and readably.
During the required drop with cables attached, a cable may become disconnected, but the cable and connector shall not break.
The selected sensor assembly shall respond observably after a few seconds of hand heating and shall respond more quickly to nearby/brief soldering-iron heating.
Verify the selected LCD/backlight combination can be read at normal laboratory viewing distance under normal indoor lighting at the intended enclosure orientation.
A connected-cable drop test passes if the cables/connectors remain unbroken and functional after reconnection even when one or more cables detach during impact.
Verify that holding each sensor in a hand produces an increasing reported temperature after a few seconds.
Verify that bringing a soldering iron near or briefly against each sensor produces an increasing reported temperature more rapidly than the hand-heating test.
When the third box is available, the connection/database path shall make the previous 300 seconds of available history usable by the web application within 10 seconds of computer-software startup.
When the computer software is already running, real-time and graph data shall become available within 10 seconds after the third box is turned ON.

The startup connection, history retrieval, history persistence, and first current-data publication path shall be implemented and tested so the required 300-second history can be served within 10 seconds when the third box is already available.
The reconnect scan interval, BLE connection setup, first current poll, and database publication shall collectively satisfy the 10-second third-box power-on recovery requirement.

The command queue polling, BLE SET_DISPLAY transaction, firmware state update, and LCD rendering path shall be tested end-to-end to complete the physical display response in less than 1 second after the computer user action.
The web interface shall display current Sensor 1 and Sensor 2 temperatures prominently using a large-font presentation when the values are valid.
The graph shall place newest data on the right, older data toward the left, add a new value once per second, and remove values that age beyond the displayed 300-second record.

The graph/main page shall render valid current temperature values in dedicated current-value elements visually larger than normal body text and immediately visible without opening settings/control views.
The graph rendering data order shall map the newest sample to the rightmost X-axis position.
On each one-second graph update, existing samples shall move logically one second farther from the right edge so older data appears to scroll left.
The graph data model shall exclude samples older than 300 seconds from the stakeholder compliance view after each update.
Physical testing of the complete -10 through +63 deg C range is not required, but the design documentation shall demonstrate that the chosen components and representations support that range.
